The fireplace isn't the problem.
The finish is.

Nearly every fireplace we're called out to is perfectly sound. It's just forty years old — orange brick, an oak mantel gone yellow, tile nobody would pick now. The finish is what dates it, so the finish is what changes.

No demolition, no dust barriers, no tearing out and rebuilding. The fireplace you have stays the fireplace you have — it just stops dating the room around it.

What we do

Brick, stone, tile and wood

01

Painted brick

The biggest change you can make to a living room in a day. Orange, blotchy or dark brick becomes one clean surface — soft white, warm grey, deep charcoal, whatever suits the room.

02

Whitewash & limewash

For when you like the texture of your brick but not the colour. A thinner, worked-in finish that lets the character underneath show through rather than covering it flat.

03

Wood mantels

Yellowed oak and tired pine restained to a deeper, more even tone, then sealed. Or painted out entirely, if the wood isn't the part you love. Either way the mantel stops fighting the rest of the room.

04

Hearths & surrounds

The raised hearth and the surround around the opening, brought in line with everything else, so the fireplace reads as one piece instead of three.

Surround, mantel and hearth face. Not inside the firebox, and no gas, venting or structural work.

How it goes

Four steps, and three are yours

  1. 01

    Send a photo

    Use the form below to tell us about your fireplace. We'll write back and let you know where to send a photo — a phone picture is plenty.

  2. 02

    Get a price

    In writing, and it covers the work, the finish and the Washington sales tax — so the number you're given is the number you pay.

  3. 03

    Pick your colour

    Samples come to you, held against your own wall in your own light. Take as long as you like — everyone does.

  4. 04

    The work gets done

    Taped off, floors covered, painted and cleaned up — with the furniture put back where it was before we leave.

How we work

Careful, and finished when we say

Fireplace Face Lifts has been refinishing brick, stone and mantels for years, and it's the only thing we do. Not a sideline of a painting business — the fireplace is the whole job.

Floors covered, furniture moved back where it was, edges taped and cut clean. And if something turns up once the work starts, you'll hear about it straight away — before it costs you anything.

Before you let anyone in

You should be able to check out anyone you hire to work inside your home. Ask for credentials and you'll get them — no hedging, no runaround.

    Ask us anything about the products we use, how we protect your floors and furniture, and how long the finish needs to cure — you'll get a straight answer.
